title: Step-by-Step Perpendicular Bisector Constructor
description: A guided construction tool where students build the perpendicular bisector of a line segment XY using only compass and straightedge. Learn mode shows 4 animated steps with sequential arc formation (arc from X draws first, then arc from Y) and measurement verification. Practice mode has 10 mixed questions: MCQ, True/False, and Fill in the Blanks with hints, explanations, and score tracking. Styled with Singularity Design System (Poppins font, #4A4DC9 purple / #FF7212 orange palette).
teaching_notes: Emphasise that compass radius must exceed half of XY for arcs to intersect. In learn mode, arcs draw sequentially (arc from X first, then arc from Y) so students can clearly see each step. Animation duration for arc steps is 3.6s for clarity. Practice mode uses shuffled mixed-type questions to reinforce conceptual understanding.
instructions_for_student: Follow the guided steps to construct the perpendicular bisector of segment XY. Watch each arc draw one at a time — first from X, then from Y. Find intersection points A and B, then draw line AB. In practice mode, test your understanding with mixed questions.

tool_objectives.instructions_for_student: Examine the line segment XY. You need to choose a compass radius that is more than half the length of XY. Why is this minimum radius necessary?
Watch carefully: first an arc is drawn from X above the line, then an arc from Y with the same radius. They intersect at point A. Notice that XA = YA — point A is equidistant from both endpoints.
Now watch the same process below the line: arc from X draws first, then arc from Y. They meet at point B. Both A and B are equidistant from X and Y.
Draw line AB. This is the perpendicular bisector! It passes through midpoint O where XO = OY, and meets XY at exactly 90 degrees.
